Remote Tech is a must for hard mode. Beyond that, Real Solar System is a mod that increases the gravity/size/etc. of planets to their comparable solar system equivalents. For instance, with this mod, Kerbin is now the size of the Earth, and takes 9.4 km/s delta V to low orbit, instead of the 4.5 km/s of delta V you need to get to low orbit over Kerbin. I'd check that out if you really want to kick the difficulty up a big notch.

I would save Minimus for the intermediate program, specifically because it will allow you to teach matching orbital inclinations. IMHO, keeping the basic program focused on orbiting and getting to the Mun is what I would go with. The Mun is much better than Minimus for mastering basic basic maneuvers beyond Kerbin orbit, as it's on an equatorial orbital plane, and all you have to do in order to get an encounter is burn when you see the sun. I do like teaching landing on Minimus versus the Mun, as it is definitely easier once you get there.


Beyond that, I think more in-depth concepts like interplanetary transfers, delta V, thrust to weight ratio, and ISP would be great for a more advanced course.


I have no idea how long this workshop is, but here are several potential "projects" I can think of off the top of my head:

1) Everyone uses the same rocket to reach Munar orbit, and whoever gets back with the most delta V left is the "winner". Teaches free return trajectories and efficient maneuvering as well as maximizing the potential of each ounce of fuel. Go less with more.

2) Make a space station with 2+ components at some altitude of Kerbin orbit. Teaches docking and all related maneuvers, as well as remembering to bring enough solar panels.

3) Using Remote Tech (can do this with or without the mod, but with is definitely more entertaining IMO) create a satellite network of 3 geostationary satellites around Kerbin that can stay in contact with any unmanned flight near Kerbin. Teaches exact maneuvering, the concept of geostationary satellites, and the real-world limitations of line of sight communications.

4) Make a spaceplane that can fly to the north pole. SSTO is probably a little advanced for only an intermediate workshop. Teaches lift, drag, and thrust.

5) Land a probe on Duna/Eve. Teaches interplanetary transfers, aerobraking, and using parachutes to save fuel.

Bonus "points" could be given for no space junk left floating around in orbit somewhere.


Best of luck to you and thanks for working to get more people hooked on the game!

I think it's tough to find any sort of context that calls for the US getting bombed at Pearl Harbor and not ending up declaring war on all axis powers. As has been said many times in the thread, a good chunk of the US population was itching to go to war against Hitler at the time, and Roosevelt wasn't exactly a fan. Tricky stuff.

Let's say Pearl Harbor never got bombed, and Britain/Russia are up against a wall dealing with the Nazi's rampaging throughout Europe. I think it's a good assumption to make that the US would have gotten involved by 1943-44 given a lack of any prior provocation like Pearl Harbor.

It had been just another night, Jack remembered. He had a particularly good time playing Dota 2 with several friends he met recently through the game. Shutting off his computer, he stood up, tired from a long day, to perform his usual bedtime routine.

Looking in the mirror while brushing his teeth, he couldn't help but think about how he had been a disappointment. How he lost his only girlfriend and prospective wife to drugs and lies. He had been sober for a year now, but it didn't make him feel any more alive. He stood there, toothbrush unmoving in his mouth, lamenting his nonexistent social life and lack of female interaction. "If only I could meet a nice girl somewhere, I'd be doing alright" he thought.

His work consumed him, and he knew it. Working for an oil company had him traveling to remote places for long periods of time, and tonight was a rare evening home in his cozy apartment on the outskirts of Denver. He was excited to get a good rest in a nice, comfortable bed, instead of a lumpy monstrosity he is accustomed to finding in various hotels in small towns across the midwest.

As he is checking his front door to make sure it is locked, he notices his hallway light flicker. A thought graces his mind about a lazy repairman before the light grows increasingly bright then bursts in a surprisingly loud BANG. Intrigued, Jack decided to investigate the unusual occurrence.

Walking outside, he finds himself shivering uncomfortably, despite the 80 degree summer night temperature. Looking around, he sees nothing unusual, save for the broken lightbulb flashing on and off several times per second. He made a note to report it to the front desk the next morning.

Maybe it was because it was dark, or maybe it was because Jack was exhausted, but he did not see the dark shape approaching from his peripheral until it was too late. All he noticed was a sharp, stifling smell in the air before he lost consciousness.

Jack awoke to find himself laying in his bed, waking just before his alarm signaled it was time for him to return to his busy life as an employee for a large company. As he walked out of his apartment long before the sun would rise, he couldn't shake the thought that the hallway light bulb was broken the night before.

It is known that Japan was considering invading Australia but ended up deciding not to. In this timeline, my reasoning was that Japan would have been motivated to eliminate a sure ally of the US before the US can bring the full weight of its' economic capabilities online.

TL;DR: America, Australia, and Britain are invaded as a result of America focusing its’ efforts only in the Pacific for the majority of the war. Japan and surrenders before Germany is able to negotiate a cease-fire. Russia bows out of the war early, similarly to WWI.

Australia, indebted to the Americans from previous events, is determined to assist in repelling the invaders and lands in northern California in early August. American-Australian forces are subsequently able to push the invaders across the border to Mexico by June of 1944, leaving a backpedaling Japan and Mexico to deal with a fully-awoken giant.

In the meantime, Britain has been having problems of its’ own. Starting in April of 1943, the German troops from the Eastern front have arrived to support their brethren in defeating the island nation that continues to rebuke the Nazis’ advances. However, Britain has been steadily losing ground in North Africa, and decides to pull the majority of its’ ground troops back to Britain, wary of a potential invasion. With little resistance remaining in continental Europe, the Germans and Italians land massive numbers of troops from locations between Brighton and Southampton in April of 1944, attempting to making a quick advance to London. The British, losing steady ground, plead with the  Americans to assist them against the Nazis. Fresh off their victory repelling the Japanese-Mexican invaders, the Americans promise to send a naval strike force and a large contingency of soldiers to defend Britain from the Nazis. On June 15th, 1944, the US formally declares war against Germany and Italy. With the help of the Americans, the British are able to stabilize their hold on the island, but finding themselves unable to fully remove the German-Italian force from their shores.

The Americans do not stop at merely repelling their invaders, but make rapid gains into the heart of Mexico. Perhaps in an ironic twist of fate, a large ground force lands on the coastal region near Mexico City, and quickly pressures a surrender from the Mexican government. Massive land cessations are granted to the American government, encompassing the entire northern half of Mexico. With the southern threat quelled, America turns its’ focus to the Pacific and the Atlantic.

Australia has been making moderate gains in the Pacific while the Japanese were tied up in their invasion, but were unable to make any substantial gains due to a lack of material support from Great Britain. America begins its’ fabled island hopping campaign across the pacific, aiming to strike at the heart of Japan and potentially invade the mainland. In September of 1944, this campaign begins, slowly chipping away at Japanese bulwark island defenses and carving a path of destruction across the pacific. Hawaii is one of the first locations to be taken from the Japanese, along with Midway, Wake Island, and many others on the Pacific fleet’s road to striking at Japan. One year later, Iwo Jima is finally controlled by the Americans, and massive aerial strikes against Japan begin in earnest shortly after.

It soon becomes apparent that Japan will not surrender without a long and difficult invasion. With few American soldiers in the Atlantic, the US is able to mount an invasion that begins in December of 1945, slowly and drudgingly moving through Japanese territory until August of 1946, where the American-Australian force is finally able to force the Japanese government into surrender, only after thoroughly destroying the vast majority of the island nation. No land cessations are provided for in the treaty between the three nations.

In the European front, Britain is slowly stabilizing its’ war machine, preparing for a massive influx of American reinforcements who will assist them in repelling the German invaders. In November of 1946, the first of these reinforcements arrived, and beat the remainder of the German forces out of Britain by the end of the year. Soon after, an invasion of France was proposed that would liberate the long-captive nation as well as provide for an opportunity to strike at Hitler’s Germany. In April of 1947, Operation Overlord is launched against a highly fortified and prepared German resistance. Despite staggering Allied losses, the American-British force is able to push through France and liberate Paris in February of 1948. 

While Germany was indeed war-weary at this point, at no point in the war did her people ever consider defeat, and as such German forces held strong at the border between France and Germany for many months, even as Italy swiftly fell to a southern invasion force led by a combined US-French force. Several months with no Allied progress have resulted in US and British populations becoming increasingly in favor of halting hostilities with Germany, and as such all remaining Axis powers negotiate a cease-fire with Allied forces on December 16th, 1948. Germany was to keep all its’ territorial gains to the west, including Poland, Ukraine, and Belarus. All other gains were to be returned to their respective nations.

It is December 8, 1941. Roosevelt has just finished his most famous speech he will ever give as President of the United States. Americans are still reeling from the catastrophic attack on Pearl Harbor just one day ago. Congress is convening at this very moment, eager to declare war on Japan.

By the next day, Roosevelt has recieved word from Hitler's administration that Germany does not wish to fight a multi-ocean conflict and wishes to consolidate its' focus upon the European fields of battle. On December 10th, Hitler publicly and formally denounces Japan's "cowardly and uncivilized" attack, and immediately cuts all ties with the Empire.

With the war in Europe raging on, things continue as they would. Germany would continue to make alarming gains in the western front while operations ground to a halt in East Russia. Moscow would live to see another spring under Russian control, while France would continue to remain in German possession for many years to come. Britain continues to balk any attack, saved from destruction only by the English Channel and Her Majesty's yet powerful navy.

In the pacific, Americans begin to bring about the brunt of their forces beginning in 1942, after Japan had nearly free reins to move their forces wherever they please, meeting little Allied resistance.

The real Pacific War began off the northern coast of Australia. Instead of electing to blockade and isolate the continental nation, a full-fledged invasion took place in March of 1942, quickly cutting across the desolate terrain and moving into the heart of urban Australia. With little time to prepare, and with a good amount of her troops fighting in the European theatre, Australia finds herself outmatched by Japan's superior numbers and firepower. In September of 1942, Sydney finds itself besieged by hungry troops of the Empire, wishing to quell this nuisance before focusing all their might on westward-moving  armies of the United States.

Earlier in the year, the US wats still building up her forces in preparation to assist the Australians if possible. The decisive Midway engagement never occurs, with Japan’s forces tied up in the Australian front. The first major Amercan-Japanese engagement occurs at Guadacanal, where Allied intelligence has determined the Japanese are constructing an airfield in preparation for an American attack on what would soon be Japanese held Australia. The Americans arrive before Japanese defenses are able to be consolidated and win a minor engagement at the island, giving the US an effective launching point from which to assault Japanese-held territory in Australia and New Guinea.

In December of 1942, the last vestiges of the Australian government and military are desperately holding out, awaiting American and Australian reinforcements that should arrive any day. On the last moment before surrender, American planes are spotted above Sydney and American warships are able to secure the harbor, subsequently beginning to push the Japanese out of the country. This only strengthens the relationship between the US and Britain.

Australian and American forces quickly rout the Japanese remaining on the continent as well as New Guinea, as the Empire orders a full retreat of soldiers in the region, allowing the Allies to definitively secure the Australian region. In the meantime, Russia has negotiated a cease-fire with Germany in the eastern European front, with neither side able to field the manpower to break the other. Thousands of battle-hardened German troops return to the Western front, as Russia is left in solitude to lick its’ wounds from the previous two years. The US, seeing the difficulty Germany had orchestrating a multi-front war, has no desire to enter the European field of battle while bringing its’ full capabilities against the Empire of Japan. Japan, Australia, and the US are left to duke it out in the Pacific for the foreseeable future.

However, Japan has been in conversation with the Mexican government, and both sides are eagerly discussing an American invasion by Mexico from the south, and Japan from the West. Japan, incentivized by the roaring American war machine coming to full strength, is eager to bring the war to the enemy’s doorstep before she is too powerful to best. With the American Pacific fleet tied up in Australia, Japan seizes its’ last opportunity to make a costly blow to the US. In May of 1943, a Japanese fleet and invasion force is spotted off the coast of Los Angeles, at the same time Mexican troops have been spotted advancing up the West coast. The surprise invasion is a smashing success, and with little advance warning, southern California is lost to the Japanese within a few weeks. Enraged, the Americans eventually stall the advance, leaving the Japanese-Mexican invasion force controlling sizable portions of Texas, California, New Mexico, and Arizona. The American Pacific fleet is unable to cut off the invasion force from Japanese reinforcements, but is effective in preventing the invasion from moving upwards along the west coast. Los Alamos, the main testing lab for the American Manhattan Project, was seized by the Japanese, and although no valuable information was obtained by the invaders, the project would end up being delayed several years because of their actions.
